The Poetry of Small Beginnings

A seed is a tiny promise. The waiting is part of its magic.

WORDS FROM THE WILD SEED CLUB

There is something almost unreasonable about trusting a seed. You hold a speck of a thing in your palm, tuck it into the earth, and imagine an entire season waiting on the other side.

The first days can be quiet. A garden asks for patience in a world that rewards instant results. You water carefully, check the light, and learn that growth is not always visible while it is happening.

When the first green curve appears, the moment is small and astonishing. Perhaps that is why people keep planting: to practice believing in beginnings they cannot yet see.

Some things bloom better when left a little wild.
